Strength development and microstructural analysis of GGBS-FCS based geopolymer concrete

Abstract:

The alarming surge in hazardous industrial waste residues and environmental issues related to Portland cement concrete have driven the development of sustainable geopolymer binders for concrete production. Due to the utilisation of aluminosilicate-rich byproducts as precursors, the dependency on cement has been reduced. Ferrochrome slag (FCS), a major byproduct from ferro-alloy plants exhibits considerable potential to be utilized as a reactive precursor. Ferrochrome slag has already been introduced in geopolymer industry mostly as coarse aggregate and fine aggregate, however its application in combination with ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) as binary precursor remains comparatively limited. The present study established the value-added utilisation of FCS and demonstrated the strength development and micro structural studies of geopolymer concrete incorporating GGBS and FCS as binary precursors. Five geopolymer alkali activated mixes were prepared by replacing GGBS with FCS at 10%,20%,30%,40% and 50%. The mechanical performance was evaluated by both destructive and non-destructive tests at different curing intervals and micro structural studies were done using Scanning Electron Microscope and Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). The evaluated strength results reported that high compressive strength of 77.2MPa was achieved with inclusion of 10% FCS, and optimum inclusion of FCS gives high compressive strength than the target strength. The formation of aluminosilicate rich gels was noticed in the SEM-EDS analysis, which attributes the development of compact and dense geopolymer matrix. The major findings concluded that using FCS as a partial replacement with GGBS valorises ferrochrome waste into high strength sustainable geopolymer concrete. &nbsp
